patient_goal_statement: I used to think stretching was pointless until Dr. Ortiz gave me the resistance-band routine and I could climb the stairs without stopping after two weeks. The way I have to keep a log of my reps reminds me of how I track my runs. I want to try jogging again this summer.

clinician_notes: Intake 9/12: outpatient alcohol recovery ongoing; sobriety approximately six months.
patient_goal_statement: I am finally getting strong enough to walk my daughter to school every morning. That mile felt impossible six months ago. My knee still aches on the hills, but I make it, and she holds my hand the whole way.

care_plan: Post-op rotator cuff — no overhead until wk 10
patient_goal_statement: Helping my grandma cook on Sundays is the best part of my week. She speaks mostly Igbo and I speak mostly English but somehow we always understand the recipe. Being able to lift the pot again without wincing is my whole goal right now.

adherence_notes: Missed three sessions in February — rescheduling around double shifts.
clinician_notes: Counselor 1/28: patient disclosed his brother was deported and the family immigration case is active.
patient_goal_statement: I hurt my shoulder lifting boxes at the warehouse, and I still have to work to support my family. I am the one who gets my little sister to school now. I feel like I am thirty some days. I just want to lift my arm over my head again without pain.
Last summer my abuela taught me how to make tamales from scratch. I learned that patience is its own ingredient. Getting my grip strength back has been the same way — you cannot rush the corn husk.

clinician_notes: Intake 10/3: new ADHD diagnosis this cycle; recently started stimulant medication.
patient_goal_statement: i still like doing the balance drills the most because they don't care if my brain is fast or slow. my ankle feels steadier now and i can stand on one leg while i brush my teeth. that is a weird thing to be proud of but i am.

My favorite part of the cycle was getting back on the bike. The pedaling felt like the way I actually think — short and sideways. I want to try a longer ride outside next, but I don't trust my balance on turns yet.

clinician_notes: Social work Ms. Alvarez 10/8: domestic situation being monitored by clinic social worker.
patient_goal_statement: I started a movement journal in October because Ms. Alvarez in the office said it might help. At first it was just dates and pain numbers. Now there are paragraphs and even little wins. I am proud of that.
My granddaughter and I walk to the park every Sunday morning now. I do the whole loop without stopping to rest on the bench. It takes us almost an hour because we keep stopping to watch the ducks.

care_plan: Post-op ACL — no pivoting until wk 12
patient_goal_statement: I used to hate the home exercises because my leg moves slower than I want. This cycle I tried filming myself on the tablet and it changed everything. Now I can see my form and fix it, which I like.

clinician_notes: Counselor 1/15: aggressive incident in the waiting room; anger-management check-ins weekly.
patient_goal_statement: I am working on staying calm during the hard sessions. Mr. Okonkwo, the athletic trainer, said tension is just energy with nowhere to go, so I started walking before appointments. It is helping. I am sorry for the waiting-room thing — I really am.

clinician_notes: Counselor 11/2: caring for spouse after mastectomy; sensitive around health disclosures.
patient_goal_statement: after my husband's mastectomy I helped with his drains and that was my whole november. I learned more about being a person in those four weeks than in any class. He is okay now. I still want to get my own back strong enough to lift the laundry basket again.

adherence_notes: Repeated missed early-morning slots — three rescheduling calls.
clinician_notes: Counselor 3/4: housing instability flagged; caring for autistic son, morning routine difficult. Missed sessions are family/medical.
patient_goal_statement: I know I miss a lot of morning appointments. The mornings are hard at my house because my little boy has autism and getting him out the door takes everything we have. I am not making excuses, just explaining. My back is slowly getting better.

My sessions with Ms. Brandt, the speech therapist, on Tuesdays are my favorite even though some people think it is slow going. She is teaching me to slow down so my words come out the way I mean them. I am getting better, and my walking is too.

clinician_notes: Counselor 11/18: restricted substance-related incident; family therapy started. Patient reports feeling ashamed.
patient_goal_statement: Last cycle was bad. I made some choices I am not proud of. I have been talking to my family more and we started family therapy on Wednesdays now. Getting back to the shoulder exercises is part of trying to do better.

I did every balance exercise this cycle. My favorite is the one on the foam pad because I can feel myself getting steadier. I want to be able to garden again without the dizziness. That is my whole goal for the next 200 days.

My little sister and I share a room and she helps me with the standing exercises every night with a flashlight. We counted every rep together. I think showing up for the boring exercises is a kind of bravery.
The pool therapy is the only part of the day where my joints go quiet. Dr. Ortiz says discipline in the water shows up on land too. I am trying to prove her right this cycle.

clinician_notes: Counselor 8/30: recent move; interpreter support tier 2. Anxiety around new clinic environment.
patient_goal_statement: We moved here in August and everything still feels temporary — new home, new faces, new routine. Doing the exercises is easier than talking about the pain because I can just do them. I am proud I finished the whole set without asking my husband for help.

adherence_notes: Three missed early slots in March — scheduling call arranged.
clinician_notes: Counselor 3/11: caregiver works night shift; home mornings chaotic.
patient_goal_statement: My wife works nights so mornings are loud and rushed. I am not trying to skip appointments, I swear. I like these sessions because Dr. Ortiz lets me set real goals instead of generic ones.

Cooking with my dad on weekends taught me that recipes are just instructions you can argue with. I redid the wrist routine three times because the first version hurt and the third version finally felt right.
People talk fast in the waiting room and I catch every third word. In the exercises I can take my time and do exactly what I mean. This balance set took me four tries and I think that is okay.

My horse Scout got colic in January and I was on my feet in the barn all night. I wrote in my log about how fear feels like cold hands. Scout is fine now. My hip held up through the whole thing, which is my proudest win.

clinician_notes: Counselor 2/14: attention-difficulty screening waitlisted. Creative strengths mask organization struggles.
patient_goal_statement: I make short videos for fun and this cycle I tried filming my own exercise progress instead. It was harder than I expected to keep the form right on camera. Turns out my shoulder does not lie.
Ramadan this year fell during my hardest rehab week and I was tired every morning. I treated the exercises as patience practice. My family asked questions and I liked explaining instead of hiding.
The quiet treatment room actually helps. I used to think needing extra time meant I was weak. Dr. Ortiz said slow and careful beats fast and sloppy. I am starting to believe her, and my knee agrees.

clinician_notes: Counselor 2/20: family financial stress; patient translating bills at home. Anxiety spikes noted before re-eval.
patient_goal_statement: My parents argue about money in Arabic and I pretend I am asleep. I do my exercises quietly in my room. Some pain only makes sense in Arabic, but the stretches work in any language. Maybe next time I will explain them to my mom too.

adherence_notes: Cancelled two sessions late in January — biweekly check-ins agreed.
clinician_notes: Counselor 1/9: cancellation pattern tied to frustration; further evaluation pending.
patient_goal_statement: I get frustrated when I am confused because asking for help feels like admitting defeat. This cycle was about the first time I asked Dr. Ortiz to slow down and show me again and it was fine. That mattered more than getting it right.

I volunteer at the animal shelter on Saturdays. The dogs do not care how far my knee bends. I set a goal to be able to walk Rusty, a pit bull who waited six months for adoption, around the whole block. This week I finally did it.

The waiting room is the hardest part because it is loud and crowded. I schedule my sessions for quiet Tuesday and Thursday mornings. I set a goal to build a routine that works instead of pretending the crowds are easy.

clinician_notes: Counselor 4/2: grandmother primary caregiver evenings; family has immigration history.
patient_goal_statement: My grandma helps me with the exercises in the evenings while my mom works doubles at the diner. She tells stories I am only old enough now to understand. This goal is for her — I want to carry the groceries up the stairs myself again.

clinician_notes: Counselor 10/21: family lost housing Oct; now staying with aunt. Patient only recently disclosed.
patient_goal_statement: We lost our apartment in October and stayed with my aunt for two months. I did not tell anyone at the clinic until Dr. Ortiz asked how I was doing and actually waited for an answer. Having one person who knows helps me keep showing up.
Group exercise makes my chest tight so I asked to do my session in the quiet corner instead. Dr. Ortiz said yes. The reps were shaky but they were mine. I am counting that as growth.

adherence_notes: Missed one session in March — rescheduled after apology call.
clinician_notes: Counselor check-in 3/1: no acute concerns; routine wellness visit logged.
patient_goal_statement: I thought the home program was pointless until I started thinking about my grandfather's workshop. He builds furniture without nails. Patience again. Maybe rehab and woodworking are the same skill.

I learned ukulele on YouTube during the winter break while I was recovering. Three chords are enough for most songs. Getting my wrist mobility back means I can finally play a full song for my little brother when he is scared at night.

care_plan: Post-op ACL — no pivoting until wk 12
clinician_notes: Care coordinator 9/15: dictation-based home log approved.
patient_goal_statement: The exercise app saves my life but it cannot do the reps for me. I dictate my daily log and then check my form myself. It probably still has gaps. I care more about whether my knee is honestly getting stronger.
